input.question: How Small Would Something Have to be in Order to Orbit Around Someone in Space?
input.ground_truth: There is no mass limit, but both the person and other object orbit the center of mass of the system. For a very light object, the center of mass will be inside the person. For heavier and heavier objects, the center of mass will gradually move farther toward the other object, until for equal mass the point is exactly in the middle. [Watch these animations](_URL_1_) to see what I mean. Based on the masses and distances of the objects, speed is the critical quantity. To orbit a 100 kg person 1 meter away circularly, a small object should move at about [80 microns/s](_URL_0_), or 1 orbit every 21.4 hours.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How Small Would Something Have to be in Order to Orbit Around Someone in Space?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a little toy ball and you’re holding it in space. If you let go of the ball gently, it will just float next to you because you’re both floating in space and there’s no air to push it away.

But if the ball is really, really tiny—like the size of a grain of sand or even smaller—and you give it a little push, it can go around you in a circle. This is called orbiting. But it has to be small enough that your gravity (the invisible pull you have because you have mass) can hold onto it, but not so big that it just flies away.

So, the smaller the ball is, the easier it is for you to keep it going around you, if you give it just the right push. But if the ball is too big, your gravity isn’t strong enough to hold it, and it will just float away.

In real life, big things like the Moon orbit the Earth because Earth’s gravity is strong enough. But if something is too small, Earth’s gravity can’t hold onto it, and it just floats away into space. So, to orbit someone in space, something has to be small enough to be held by their gravity, but not so small that it just zooms away or gets pushed around by other things.
